ai.literal: By the fate of accruing (wealth), there arises the absence of sloth; by the fate of wealth in hand departing, there arises laziness.
ai.translation: Through the destiny of prosperity, untiring effort arises; through the destiny of losing one's wealth, laziness takes hold.
ai.modern: செல்வம் சேர்வதற்குக் காரணமான விதியினால் சோர்வில்லாத முயற்சி உண்டாகும்; கையில் உள்ள பொருள் அழிவதற்குக் காரணமான விதியினால் சோம்பல் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how destiny (ஊழ்) shapes a person's mental attitude and drive. When it is one's destiny to prosper (ஆகூழ்), an innate sense of untiring effort and perseverance (அசைவின்மை) arises, driving them to work hard. Conversely, when destiny decrees the loss of one's wealth (போகூழ்), laziness and apathy (மடி) naturally creep in, causing them to neglect their work. Thus, the author suggests that even our industriousness or laziness is directed by the unseen force of destiny.

ai.literal: The fate of loss will cause ignorance; the fate of gaining, when occurred, will expand knowledge.
ai.translation: The destiny of loss makes one foolish, whereas the destiny of gain, when it arrives, expands one's wisdom.
ai.modern: இழப்பைத் தரும் ஊழ்வினை ஒருவனை அறிவற்றவனாக ஆக்கும்; ஆக்கத்தைத் தரும் ஊழ்வினை வந்து சேரும்போது, அது அவனது அறிவை விரிவடையச் செய்யும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how destiny influences human intellect. When a person is destined to suffer loss, their mind is clouded by ignorance, leading them to make poor decisions. Conversely, when the destiny of prosperity and gain arrives, it naturally expands their wisdom, enabling them to think clearly and succeed. Thus, the power of destiny shapes even the sharpness of one's intellect.

ai.literal: Subtle treatises many even if one learns, yet one's own innate intellect indeed will prevail.
ai.translation: Even if a person studies many subtle and profound treatises, their own innate intellect, shaped by destiny, will ultimately prevail.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் நுட்பமான பல நூல்களைக் கற்றாலும், அவருடைய இயற்கையான அறிவே மேலோங்கி நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how destiny influences a person's intellect and behavior. Even if someone acquires vast knowledge by studying highly sophisticated and subtle treatises, their innate understanding ('uṇmai aṟivu') will ultimately dominate. Here, 'uṇmai' refers to the natural, fundamental disposition of the mind as determined by one's destiny. Thus, external learning cannot easily override the core nature ordained by fate.

ai.literal: Two different are the world's nature: wealth is different, and becoming clear-minded is different.
ai.translation: The way of the world is of two different kinds: acquiring wealth is one thing, and becoming wise and clear-minded is quite another.
ai.modern: உலகத்தின் இயல்பு இரு வேறுபட்ட தன்மைகளைக் கொண்டது; செல்வம் பெறுவது ஒரு வகை, அறிவுத் தெளிவு உடையவர் ஆவது மற்றொரு வகை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the dual nature of worldly fortune, which separates material wealth from intellectual clarity. The word 'திரு' refers to wealth or prosperity, while 'தெள்ளியர்' refers to those who possess clear, wise minds. The poet points out that these two qualities do not naturally go together in this world. One may have immense wealth but lack wisdom, or possess great wisdom but remain poor. The repetition of 'வேறு' emphasizes that these two states are governed by entirely different laws of destiny.

ai.literal: Good things all bad will become; even bad things good will become, wealth for making.
ai.translation: In the endeavor to acquire wealth, all good efforts turn into harmful ones when fate is adverse, and even unfavorable things turn into beneficial ones when fate is favorable.
ai.modern: செல்வத்தைச் சேர்க்கும் முயற்சியில், நல்லவை எல்லாம் தீமையாக மாறும்; தீமையானவைகளும் நன்மையாக மாறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how fate completely alters the outcomes of one's efforts to acquire wealth. When fate is unfavorable, even the most well-planned, positive, and good actions turn into failures or cause harm. Conversely, when fate is favorable, even mistakes, obstacles, or seemingly bad circumstances turn around to produce successful and good results. Thus, the ultimate success in acquiring wealth depends not just on the nature of the actions themselves, but on the underlying power of fate.

ai.literal: Even if protected, they will not become [one's own], those which are not [one's] destiny; having carried and poured out, they will not go away, those which are one's own.
ai.translation: Even if one guards them with care, things that are not destined to be one's own will not remain; even if one carries them away and throws them out, things that are destined to be one's own will not leave.
ai.modern: விதிப்படி நமக்கு உரியவை அல்லாத பொருள்களை நாம் போற்றிப் பாதுகாத்தாலும் அவை நம்மிடம் தங்க மாட்டா; நமக்கு உரிய பொருள்களை நாம் கொண்டுபோய்க் கொட்டினாலும் அவை நம்மை விட்டுப் போகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the absolute power of destiny over material possessions. The author explains that what is not destined to be ours cannot be retained, no matter how much effort we put into guarding and protecting it. Conversely, what is destined to be ours cannot be lost; even if we actively try to discard or throw it away, it will find its way back to us and will not leave. Through these contrasting actions of guarding and discarding, the couplet emphasizes that human effort is ultimately subordinate to the laws of destiny.

ai.literal: Other than the way He who apportioned has apportioned, to those who have gathered ten million, enjoying is difficult.
ai.translation: Except in the way ordained by the Apportioner, it is difficult even for those who have amassed millions to enjoy their wealth.
ai.modern: வகுத்தவன் வகுத்துக் கொடுத்த வழியிலல்லாமல், கோடிக்கணக்கான பொருள்களைச் சேர்த்து வைத்தவர்களுக்கும் அவற்றை அனுபவிப்பது கடினமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme power of destiny over human possession and effort. The word 'வகுத்தான்' refers to the Apportioner, the force that pre-ordains each individual's share of experiences. Even if a person succeeds in accumulating immense wealth, represented here by 'கோடி' (ten million), they cannot enjoy ('துய்த்தல்') it unless it is in the manner ('வகை') allotted to them. Thus, the poet emphasizes that possession does not guarantee enjoyment, as our experiences are ultimately governed by destiny.

ai.literal: They would renounce indeed, those who lack enjoyments, if things destined to happen would pass away without making them experience.
ai.translation: Those who lack the means of enjoyment would surely renounce the world, if only destined events would pass away without forcing them to experience their fruits.
ai.modern: அனுபவிக்க வேண்டிய விதிப்பயன்கள் தங்களை அனுபவிக்கச் செய்யாமல் சும்மா கடந்து போய்விடுமானால், நுகர்பொருள்கள் இல்லாத ஏழைகள் உலகத்தைத் துறந்து துறவிகளாகிவிடுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the inescapable power of destiny. The poet suggests that those who suffer from a lack of basic resources and enjoyments ('tuppuravu illār') would easily renounce worldly life ('tuṟappār') to escape their misery. However, they are unable to do so because destiny ('uṟaṟpāla') does not pass away ('kaḻiyum') without forcing them to experience ('ūṭṭā') the fruits of their past actions. Thus, even the desire to renounce is governed and restricted by destiny, binding individuals to their destined experiences.

words.gloss: adversity or the opposite of good

ai.literal: When good fortune occurs, those who experience it as good things; when adversity occurs, experiencing distress, why?
ai.translation: Why should those who gladly accept prosperity as a good thing when it comes, grieve and suffer distress when adversity comes?
ai.modern: நன்மை வரும்போது அதனை நல்லதாக ஏற்றுக்கொள்பவர்கள், தீமை வரும்போது மட்டும் துன்பப்பட்டு வருந்துவது ஏன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet points out the inconsistency in how people respond to the inevitable cycles of destiny. When good fortune (நன்று) arrives, people readily welcome and enjoy it as something natural and good (நல்லவா காண்பவர்). However, when the opposite—misfortune or adversity (அன்று)—strikes, they fall into deep grief and distress (அல்லல் படுவது). The poet asks 'why' (எவன்) they do this, suggesting that since both joy and sorrow are governed by the same law of destiny, one should maintain equanimity and accept both with an equal mind.

ai.literal: Than fate, what things of great power exist? Even if one plans another way, itself will stand ahead.
ai.translation: What is of greater power than fate? Even if one plans another way to bypass it, fate itself will arrive first and stand ahead.
ai.modern: ஊழை விடப் பெரிய வலிமை உடையவை வேறு எவை உள்ளன? அதைத் தடுப்பதற்கு வேறு ஒரு வழியை ஆராய்ந்து திட்டமிட்டாலும், ஊழ் தானே முந்திக்கொண்டு வந்து நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet asserts the supreme power of fate over human designs. The author rhetorically asks what could possibly possess greater strength than fate. Even if a person tries to devise an alternative plan or countermeasure to bypass it, fate itself will anticipate that move and manifest beforehand. The key words 'சூழினும்' (even if planned) and 'முந்துறும்' (will stand ahead) highlight the futility of trying to outsmart destiny, as the very attempt is forestalled by fate.
